title: Fix some warnings flagged by checking scripts

notes.body: assigned to @martin.r.mathieson
approved this merge request
enabled automatic add to merge train when checks pass

I'm not sure how to regenerate the corba dissectors?

At the top level of the <build> folder:
'make corba-dissectors'
doesn't do anything

Similarly if I go to <build>/epan/dissectors/corba-idl
And run 'make' there, nothing happens.  Couldn't force it with 'make clean'..

In order to regenerate the CORBA dissectors, the omniidl executable from omniORB has to be found. There is a Windows package, though I haven't looked into it: https://omniorb.sourceforge.io/

I have only done it from Linux by installing a package.
I do (now) have omniidl on my path, final insult was needing to rerun cmake :smile:
Yeah, it probably cached that it couldn't find it so you might have needed to erase the cache.
The Corba "idl2wrs" script is a simple wrapper that just calls omniidl with a command line option or two that I setup the CMake command to do directly.

It looks like there is an vcpkg port for OmniORB: https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/be2e197ea5bc32028dad3c651053ed926d91a2d7/ports/omniorb so we might be able to provide it as an artifact through https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-development-libraries

@geraldcombs what do you think?

Sounds fine to me. It looks like the port [only supports x64](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/be2e197ea5bc32028dad3c651053ed926d91a2d7/ports/omniorb/vcpkg.json#L8), but that shouldn't be a problem in this case.

Since we have two things called `idl2wrs` (CORBA and a DCERPC one), I've been a little inclined to try to get rid of the CORBA one, as it's just a simple wrapper, and try to steer development towards using omniidl and the CMake target directly.
